capability: Require explicit Registry lifecycle implementations and restore checks cancelled by their caller
searchEvidence: Independent R2 review found default interface bodies silently turned missing Registry implementations into ordinary CheckAsync or NotConfigured results
The same review found caller cancellation could leave the owned check and published snapshot in Checking state
Legacy/manual and fixed-Registry checks already share one generation and cancellation field, so cleanup belongs to one shared partial-class helper
semanticOwner: VersionManagementExperience explicitly implements every IVersionManagementExperience use case and RestoreCancelledCheck owns caller-cancellation cleanup for both direct-source and Registry checks
terminalContract: Every implementation must declare Resume and self-test behavior. Caller cancellation propagates, restores the exact prior published snapshot, disposes only the caller-owned check, performs no durable write, and permits a clean subsequent check.

designReview.evidence: The exact-head R2 and minimality review required removing two silent default semantic implementations and adding one shared cancellation cleanup path with direct and Registry regression evidence.
